summary: Two static release defects: singleton triple input bypasses FFM/FRM, including the profiler input; RGB-only missing-modality reconstruction omits single-source Softmax. Historical benchmark effects not established.
reviewed_version: PMLR 267 proceedings PDF and MFRNet commit ec54a1302321cda4b5fad9ca1c0878dabf0b46b6
page_convention: 1-based PDF pages equal local printed pages 1–12

problems.title: Singleton batch bypasses both proposed modules
problems.claim: Sections 3.1–3.2 and Figure 2 describe FFM and FRM as components; Table 4 reports model computational cost.
assumptions: Configured ViT-B-16, GEN=True, ADA=True, PROMPT=False, ADAPTER=False
problems.check: Concatenation gives B=3b. Both FFM and final-block FRM require B>3. With b=1 guards are false; b=2 makes them true. Released flops() constructs b=1 inputs.
problems.result: Singleton forward and completed profiler trace use the bypass architecture.
counterevidence: No singleton remainder was established for published data
problems.core_dependency: The released computation of the proposed core modules is bypassed for the scoped execution case; historical paper-level efficiency damage is unresolved.
problems.impact: Minor release-specific deployment/profiling discrepancy. Does not prove published performance or efficiency scores false.

correction.proposal: Remove architecture choice based on batch cardinality and validate singleton MoE execution; profile enabled modules

problems.title: RGB-only reconstruction omits weight normalization
problems.claim: Section 3.1 normalizes source weights via Softmax and equation (6) reconstructs from available modalities.
assumptions: At least two triples so FFM enabled
problems.check: Choose linear weight zero and bias -1. Raw code returns -g while single-source Softmax returns g. Independent intermediate example g=(1,2) yields (-1,-2) versus (1,2).
problems.result: Released nt branch is algebraically asymmetric with the normalized rn and rt branches.
counterevidence: Equation (6) does not repeat renormalization explicitly
A trained raw weight could equal one
No checkpoint behavior or historical Table 3 provenance established
The example is an intermediate computation, not a trained-network reproduction
problems.core_dependency: Missing-modality reconstruction branch only; full empirical conclusions not disproved.
problems.impact: Minor release-specific mismatch; empirical effect unresolved.

correction.verification: Scalar identity checked; full model and accuracy untested

limitations: Separate OpenReview attachments unavailable in packet

P1.original_and_conditions: Independently read physical PDF pp.3-4, section 3.1, Figure 2 and section 3.2; matched configured ViT-B-16 GEN/ADA=True and PROMPT/ADAPTER=False. Read actual fixed-commit model.py:351-362,676-688,771-779 and wrapper:72-92,137-164.
P1.decisive_calculation: The wrapper concatenates three b-sized tensors, hence B=3b. For b=1, B=3 fails both strict >3 guards. For b=2, B=6 satisfies both. The profiler creates three leading-dimension-one inputs. This is an algebraic branch check, with no author execution.
P1.counterevidence: A profiler may fail earlier at cam_label processing, so the report correctly conditions its trace claim on completion. Default evaluation b=128 enables modules; neither a singleton published-data remainder nor the historical Table 4 call is established.
P1.dependency_severity_repair: Two advertised core modules are omitted on a bounded release path. Minor is supported for release-specific inference/profiling, without inferring false historical scores. Removing guards remains untested for singleton Tutel compatibility; no replacement FLOP count is certified.

P2.original_and_conditions: Physical pp.3-4 explicitly apply Softmax to reconstructed weights; Eq.(6) then restricts available sources. Actual code Gen_lack_weight is pooling plus unconstrained linear output; rn/rt cases normalize while nt lines 864-869 do not. Assumed b>=2 keeps FFM enabled.
P2.decisive_calculation: With zero linear weights and bias -1, raw coefficient=-1 for any input; one-source Softmax coefficient=exp(-1)/exp(-1)=1. Thus nonzero intermediate g=(1,2) yields (-1,-2) versus (1,2). No trained-checkpoint or full-network claim is needed.
P2.counterevidence: Eq.(6) does not repeat renormalization, but explicit prior Softmax and symmetric release cases substantiate the stated normalized interpretation. A learned raw value exactly one can coincide locally; it does not establish functional equivalence.
P2.dependency_severity_repair: Minor single RGB-only release branch, with unknown empirical size/provenance. One-element Softmax restores only the claimed intermediate algebra; accuracy and end-to-end behavior remain unverified.
